curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42075-1-2.pdf (book 2 builds the First Responder, its functions on pages 112-113); book 1, omr/instructions/42075-1-1.pdf, builds the alternate hot rod

functions.does: The black gear on the cab roof steers the front wheels: its upright shaft turns a long shaft forward through bevel gears, and two 16 tooth gears, by way of an idler that rides loose on the drive shaft, turn the pinion on the front steering rack.
functions.source: book 2: steps 9-21 and 50 (the arrows on the roof gear and the steering), page 113 (top left photo)

functions.does: Pushed along, the rear wheels drive the two cylinder engine under the bonnet: a differential on the rear axle turns a drive shaft with a universal joint forward to the front, where a 20 tooth gear turns the crankshaft and the two pistons slide in and out of their cylinders.
functions.source: book 2: steps 36-41 (differential), 49-52 (drive shaft), 117-122 (engine); page 113 (top left photo, the arrow on the front wheel)

functions.does: The front wheels roll freely; only the rear ones are driven.
The gear on the front bumper winds the winch, reeling the hook's string in or out.
functions.source: book 2: steps 103-107 (the reel, string and hook), page 113 (bottom left photo)

functions.does: The rear axle is a swinging, sprung unit: it pivots at its front end and a single shock absorber above the differential lets it rise and fall.
functions.source: book 2: steps 33-49 (the axle frame and its pivot), page 113 (top right photo, the arrows on the rear wheels)
functions.note: the shock's spring only matters under the truck's weight; the axle's travel is what's checked

functions.does: The light mast, lying along the roof, swings up at the back of the truck to stand upright with its lamp on top.
functions.source: book 2: pages 112 and 113 (bottom right photo, the arrow on the mast)

functions.does: The bonnet, with the grille and headlights, tips up and forward to show the engine.
functions.source: book 2: step 137 (the bonnet fitted on its hinge), page 112 (inset, the arrow on the bonnet)
inferred: the inset on page 112 draws a curved arrow beside a blue seat; what it means isn't spelt out
